source_text: Ta is discipulus spiritalis vere recipiens Spiritum Dei, qui ab initio in universis dispositionibus Dei adfuit hominibus, et futura annuntiavit et preesentia ostendit et preeterita enarrat, judicat quidem omnes, ipse autem a nemine judicatur. Nam judicat gentes, creature magis quam Oreatori servientes, et reprobabili mente universam suam operationem in vanum consumentes. Judicat autem etiam Judos, non percipientes verbum libertatis, neque volentes abire liberos, cum habeant preesentem liberatorem ; sed intempestive extra legem servire simulantes nihil indigenti Deo, et Christi adventum, quem propter salutem hominum fecit, non cognoseentes, neque intelligere volentes, quoniam duos adventus ejus omnes annuntiaverunt prophetee: unum quidem, in homo in plaga factus est, sciens ferre imbecillitatem, et in pullo asinee sedens, et reprobatus lapis ab eedificantibus, et sicut ovis ad victimam adductus, et per extensionem manuum dissolvens quidem Amalech; congregans autem dispersos filios a terminis terre in ovile Patris, et recommemoratus mortuorum suorum qui dormierant, et descendens ad eos, uti erueret eos®; secundum autem, in quo super nubes veniet, superducens diem que est sicut clibanus ardens, et percutiens terram verbo oris sui, et spiritu per labia sua interficiens impios, et ventilabrum in manu habens, et’ emundans aream suam, et triticum quidem in horreum comburens autem paleas igne inexstinguibili.
pass_a_gloss: The spiritual disciple truly receiving the Spirit of God, who from the beginning in all dispositions of God was present to men, and announced future things and showed present things and narrated past things, judges indeed all, but is judged by no one. For he judges the nations, creatures serving the creature more than the Creator, and with a reprobate mind consuming their whole operation in vain. And he judges also the Jews, not perceiving the word of liberty, nor willing to depart free, when they have a present liberator; but simulating to serve outside the law in an unseasonable manner, being in no need of God, and not recognizing the advent of Christ, which he made for the salvation of men, nor willing to understand, since all the prophets announced two advents of him: one indeed, in which he was made in the flesh, knowing to bear infirmity, and sitting on a foal of an ass, and a stone rejected by the builders, and led as a sheep to sacrifice, and dissolving Amalech by the extension of his hands; gathering however the dispersed sons from the ends of the earth into the fold of the Father, and being reminded of his dead who slept, and descending to them, so that he might raise them; but the second, in which he will come upon the clouds, bringing a day which is like a burning furnace, and striking the earth with the word of his mouth, and slaying the impious with the spirit through his lips, and having a winnowing fan in his hand, and purifying his floor, and gathering the wheat into the granary, but burning the chaff with inextinguishable fire.

pass_b_english: The true spiritual disciple receives the Spirit of God. From the beginning the Spirit was present to humanity in every arrangement of God. He announced the future, revealed the present, and narrated the past. He judges all things, yet no one judges him.

For he judges the nations—creatures who serve the creature rather than the Creator, consuming their entire effort in vain with a depraved mind (Rom 1:25). He also judges the Jews, who do not perceive the word of liberty nor wish to go free, even though their Liberator stands present among them. They pretend to serve outside the law at the wrong time, as if God needed anything, and they refuse to recognize or understand Christ's advent, which he accomplished for human salvation. All the prophets foretold two advents of his (Acts 3:18).

In the first, he was made flesh, knowing how to bear weakness. He sat upon a donkey's colt (Zech 9:9). He became the stone the builders rejected (Ps 118:22). He was led like a sheep to slaughter. By stretching out his hands he dissolved Amalek. He gathered the scattered children from the ends of the earth into the Father's fold. He remembered his dead who slept, and descended to them so that he might raise them.

But the second advent will be different: he will come upon the clouds, bringing a day that burns like a furnace. He will strike the earth with the word of his mouth and slay the wicked with the breath of his lips (Isa 11:4). He will hold a winnowing fork in his hand, clear his threshing floor, gather the wheat into his barn, and burn the chaff with unquenchable fire (Matt 3:12).

review.notes: The translation accurately captures the Latin text. Pass A provides a faithful clause-by-clause translation. Pass B provides a fluent rendering that includes necessary biblical citations for the allusions (Zech 9:9, Ps 118:22, Isa 11:4, Matt 3:12) which are required by the instructions for handling scripture-alluding passages. The Latin 'in pullo asinee sedens' is rendered as 'sat upon a donkey's colt' in Pass B, which is a correct identification of the Zechariah 9:9 allusion.
